    Tutorial: from raw EEG to ERD/ERS and decoding¶

    This notebook walks through the eegkit building blocks on subject 1 of the PhysioNet EEGBCI motor-imagery dataset (imagining closing the left vs. right fist, 3 runs, 64 channels, 160 Hz). Every step is also what eegkit run does for all subjects.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from eegkit import viz
from eegkit.analysis import (band_erders, band_power_table, compute_erders,
                             compute_psd_by_condition, decode_csp_lda)
from eegkit.config import Config
from eegkit.epochs import make_epochs, reject_epochs
from eegkit.io import load_subject
from eegkit.preprocess import preprocess

DATA = next(p for p in (Path("data/raw"), Path("../data/raw")) if p.exists())
cfg = Config()          # defaults; see configs/default.yaml
raw = load_subject(1, cfg.runs, DATA)
raw

    1. Look at the raw signal¶

    Cue markers (dashed) are the left/right imagery onsets.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    names = ["C3", "Cz", "C4", "FC3", "FC4", "Oz"]
picks = [raw.ch_names.index(c) for c in names]
sf = raw.info["sfreq"]
marks = [(o, "left" if d == "T1" else "right")
         for o, d in zip(raw.annotations.onset, raw.annotations.description) if d != "T0"]
viz.plot_traces(raw.get_data(picks=picks, start=0, stop=int(20 * sf)),
                np.arange(int(20 * sf)) / sf, names, 150, marks);

    2. Preprocess¶

    Band-pass 1-40 Hz, 60 Hz notch, robust bad-channel detection (flat / high variance), average reference. Every function returns a copy.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    clean, bads = preprocess(raw, cfg.preprocess)
print("flat:", bads.flat, " noisy:", bads.noisy)
    clean, bads = preprocess(raw, cfg.preprocess) print("flat:", bads.flat, " noisy:", bads.noisy)
    flat: []  noisy: []

    3. Epoch and reject artifacts¶

    Epochs span -1.5...4.5 s around each cue; rejection looks at the sensorimotor channels.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    epochs = make_epochs(clean, cfg.epochs.tmin, cfg.epochs.tmax, cfg.epochs.baseline)
epochs, report = reject_epochs(epochs, cfg.epochs.reject_uv, cfg.epochs.reject_channels)
print(report)
epochs

    4. Spectra and band power¶

    5. ERD/ERS¶

    Percent power change relative to the -1...0 s baseline: negative = event-related desynchronization (ERD). The brief red patch right after the cue is the evoked response, not an ERS.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    erd = compute_erders(epochs)
viz.plot_erders(erd);
    erd = compute_erders(epochs) viz.plot_erders(erd);

    Copied! 
    {cond: {k: round(v) for k, v in band_erders(r, (8, 13)).items()} for cond, r in erd.items()}

    7. Decoding left vs right¶

    CSP spatial filters + LDA, 5-fold stratified cross-validation; filters are fitted inside each training fold only.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    res = decode_csp_lda(epochs, channels=cfg.analysis.decoding.channels)
print(f"accuracy {res.accuracy:.2f} +/- {res.std:.2f}  over {res.n_epochs} epochs", res.fold_scores)
    res = decode_csp_lda(epochs, channels=cfg.analysis.decoding.channels) print(f"accuracy {res.accuracy:.2f} +/- {res.std:.2f} over {res.n_epochs} epochs", res.fold_scores)
    accuracy 0.78 +/- 0.16  over 45 epochs [0.7777777777777778, 1.0, 0.8888888888888888, 0.5555555555555556, 0.6666666666666666]

    8. The same signal, online¶

    Replay the recording through the simulated amplifier (8x faster than real time here) and compute sliding-window band power at C3/C4 as a real-time system would.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    import time
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from eegkit.realtime import MockAmplifier, OnlineProcessor

amp = MockAmplifier.from_raw(clean, speed=8.0, loop=False, chunk_samples=16)
proc = OnlineProcessor(amp.ch_names, amp.sfreq, window_s=1.0, hop_s=0.25)
out = []
amp.start(); proc.run(amp, out.append)       # blocks until the finite stream ends
t = np.array([r.time_s for r in out])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3))
for chn, col in (("C3", "#009E73"), ("C4", "#CC79A7")):
    ax.plot(t, [r.powers[chn]["mu"] * 1e12 for r in out], color=col, label=f"{chn} mu")
for s, lab in amp._markers:
    ax.axvline(s / amp.sfreq, color=viz.COLORS[lab], alpha=.35, lw=1)
ax.set(xlabel="Stream time (s)", ylabel="Mu power (uV^2)", xlim=(0, 125)); ax.legend(frameon=False)
print(f"{proc.stats.windows} windows, mean latency {1e3*np.mean(proc.stats.latencies):.1f} ms,",
      "status:", proc.stats.status)
    import time import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from eegkit.realtime import MockAmplifier, OnlineProcessor amp = MockAmplifier.from_raw(clean, speed=8.0, loop=False, chunk_samples=16) proc = OnlineProcessor(amp.ch_names, amp.sfreq, window_s=1.0, hop_s=0.25) out = [] amp.start(); proc.run(amp, out.append) # blocks until the finite stream ends t = np.array([r.time_s for r in out]) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3)) for chn, col in (("C3", "#009E73"), ("C4", "#CC79A7")): ax.plot(t, [r.powers[chn]["mu"] * 1e12 for r in out], color=col, label=f"{chn} mu") for s, lab in amp._markers: ax.axvline(s / amp.sfreq, color=viz.COLORS[lab], alpha=.35, lw=1) ax.set(xlabel="Stream time (s)", ylabel="Mu power (uV^2)", xlim=(0, 125)); ax.legend(frameon=False) print(f"{proc.stats.windows} windows, mean latency {1e3*np.mean(proc.stats.latencies):.1f} ms,", "status:", proc.stats.status)
